rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all 10 compounds while retaining early-eluting components. This mid-temperature scouting run will reveal critical separations and guide subsequent gradient and temperature adjustments.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin survives. Keeping temperature and endpoints fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness.

Test temperature-driven selectivity changes to separate the crowded central peaks without lengthening the gradient. The fast gradient already eliminates the time penalty, so improving its critical resolutions could approach the maximum score.

Use a slightly shallower gradient to improve central-peak resolution, with temperature just below 60 °C to move away from the near-coelution seen there. The last peak should remain near the zero-time-penalty window.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness to test whether the narrow resolution margins improve while retaining zero time penalty. Injection 4 already achieved the maximum CRF; this explores a nearby alternative with potentially stronger separation.

Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution times and assess its effect on the two marginal separations. The maximum CRF is already secured; this explores whether a faster alternative can match it.

Slightly flatten injection 6's gradient to recover resolution of its sole under-resolved pair while preserving the improved separation of the other critical pair. This may match the maximum CRF with a better-balanced resolution margin.

Flatten the gradient one more grid step to bring the remaining critical pair above 1.5 while keeping the other near 1.6. The projected last-peak time is approximately 8 minutes, potentially retaining zero time penalty and matching the maximum CRF.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with the fast gradient to seek another fully resolved, zero-time-penalty method. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this tests a distinct operating region rather than further tuning marginal separations at 55 °C.

Combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to seek stronger critical-pair separation without extending the last-peak time beyond approximately 8 minutes. This follows the successful shift from injection 5 to injection 8, which improved minimum resolution while maintaining maximum CRF.

Test the temperature sensitivity of the maximum-scoring method by lowering temperature one grid step. This will establish whether full resolution and zero time penalty extend to a nearby temperature setting.

Preserve injection 4's successful gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint and shortening the programmed gradient. Since all peaks previously eluted before 10 minutes, this should retain maximum CRF, provided the lower endpoint adequately elutes the mixture.

Use a gradient slope between injections 7 and 8 to target both critical resolutions above 1.5 while bringing the last peak below 8 minutes. This may match the maximum CRF with a slightly better resolution margin than injection 4.

Keep the successful gradient slope of injections 4 and 12 while reducing the endpoint and programmed duration again. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends at the column outlet, potentially preserving maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Maintain the maximum-scoring gradient slope through the first nine peaks, then hold at a lower final organic fraction. This tests whether the isolated last peak still elutes soon enough to preserve zero time penalty and maximum CRF.

Test whether higher starting organic at 60 °C moves the previously near-coeluting central pair apart after an elution-order change. With maximum CRF already achieved, this explores a distinctly faster alternative rather than another equivalent gradient slope.

Steepen injection 16's gradient to test whether the central pair separates further on its new elution-order branch. This could yield a substantially faster maximum-scoring method, though the neighboring separations must also remain above 1.5.

Increase starting organic to test whether the remaining central near-coelution separates further, while restoring the longer gradient to protect its neighboring pair. This explores a faster maximum-CRF alternative while checking that the earliest peaks remain adequately resolved.

Use a slightly shallower gradient than injection 8 to improve its earlier critical separation while checking that the minimum resolution remains above 1.5. The projected last-peak time is about 8.2 minutes, within the zero-penalty range demonstrated by injection 15.

Use a shallower gradient than injection 10 to improve its sole under-resolved pair while retaining its stronger separation of the other critical pair. This tests whether a higher-starting-organic method can match maximum CRF with better resolution margins before a time penalty appears.

Slightly flatten injection 20's gradient to raise its sole under-resolved pair above 1.5 while preserving the other critical separation. The last peak is projected near 9 minutes, testing whether improved resolution can still coincide with zero time penalty.

Preserve injection 8's gradient slope and temperature while reducing the endpoint and programmed duration. Its last peak eluted before this gradient would end at the outlet, so this method should retain the maximum CRF and its 1.58 minimum resolution.

Slightly flatten injection 22's gradient to strengthen the earlier critical separation while testing whether the other remains above 1.5. The last peak should elute near the demonstrated zero-time-penalty window, potentially preserving maximum CRF at a lower endpoint.

Test a gradient slope between the maximum-scoring injections 19 and 23, targeting full resolution with the last peak comfortably below 9 minutes. This should provide another maximum-CRF option with a lower endpoint than injection 19.

Finish with a gradient slope bracketed by maximum-scoring injections 23 and 24, where full resolution and zero time penalty are expected. The campaign has already reached the theoretical maximum CRF of 1.000; this final run tests another nearby operating point.
